mission: HEADROOM PHASE-4 - VERIFICATION-AWARE RUNTIME GATE, MIGRATION STEPS 1+2 (envelope interface + Phase-3 resolver, no gating)

whatWasBuilt.envelopeTypes: lib/contract-model/runtime/verification-envelope.ts - types, the policy vocabulary, and DETECTION-ONLY identity helpers. Its header states in block capitals that nothing in it gates anything.
whatWasBuilt.resolver: lib/contract-model/verification-envelope/resolver.ts - an ADAPTER package, in neither core layer
whatWasBuilt.plumbing: optional verification?/policy? on the entry types, plus EvaluationContext.unitId and an Env.unitId that follows the owner as the evaluator expands into a referenced definition or rule

layeringCorrection.whatIHadDone: the resolver was first placed under compiler/semantic-verification/ with a type-only import of the runtime envelope types, on the reasoning that `import type` erases and creates no runtime edge
layeringCorrection.whatCaughtIt: two existing architecture invariants - runtime/anti-enumeration.test.ts's `no Phase-3 compiler or IR module imports the Phase-4 runtime` (a grep over compiler/ and ir/, which a type-only import still trips) and capacity/determinism-and-generality.test.ts's pinned intra-runtime import list
layeringCorrection.whyTheTestWasRight: the invariant is about which layer may know the other exists, not about what survives compilation. A type-only import still encodes that knowledge in the source.
layeringCorrection.resolution: the resolver moved to lib/contract-model/verification-envelope/ - an adapter that depends on BOTH compiler types and runtime types, while compiler/ and runtime/ stay ignorant of each other. The invariant grep is clean. The capacity pin gained one entry, ../verification-envelope, which is an intra-runtime import and still satisfies that test's own semantic check (nothing from compiler/).

inertnessProof.method: scripts/phase-4-inertness-probe.ts drives evaluateExpression, buildDependencyGraph, evaluateRule over six sufficiency shapes, buildCapacityGraph and evaluateCapacityState across fixed fixtures, serializes every field the runtime returns and prints one sha256. The runtime emits no wall-clock field, which is what makes the comparison exact rather than approximate.
inertnessProof.whyUnitIdIsInvisible: provenance carries ruleId/definitionId only; unitId is never serialized, and Env is internal

envelopePresentButInert.setup: a COMPLETE rule whose capacity is PERCENT(1), with a resolved envelope carrying a NODE-scoped MATERIAL finding on that exact node, passed with policy REQUIRE
envelopePresentButInert.result: byte-identical to omitting the envelope; status EXECUTABLE
envelopePresentButInert.interimCondition: this is deliberate and temporary. Step 3 inverts it.

resolverRules.acceptedPathDialect: ^(rules|definitions|sharedCapacities)\\[\\d+\\]((\\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(\\[\\d+\\])?)*)$ - concrete indices only, no fuzzy fallback
resolverRules.rootIndexIgnoredDeliberately: the root's INDEX is positional and is ignored; binding is by ruleOrDefinitionId. The root's KIND is checked, so a definitions[...] path on a rule is UNIT_WRONG_ROOT_KIND.
neverDone: hopping from a landed non-expression (a description, a sufficiency value) to a nearby sibling that happens to have one
resolverRules.determinism: units sorted by id; findings sorted NODE-before-UNIT then by findingId; exprIds sorted and de-duplicated; no reliance on map or object iteration order

corpusResolution.differenceFromTheDesignEstimate: the design estimated 498 MATERIAL findings with 208 machine-resolvable. Only 87 of the 498 could be RESOLVED at all, because 411 name a ruleOrDefinitionId whose compiled IR object is not preserved alongside the verification result in the same artifact. That is a corpus-preservation gap, not a resolver defect - the estimate counted findings whose path LOOKED parseable, while the resolver must also find the node. Of the 87 that could be bound, 61% resolved to an exact node, which is better than the 42% the path-shape estimate implied.
corpusResolution.strongIdentityIsZero: every preserved unit has a null sourceContentVersion, exactly as the design warned. Every envelope built from this corpus is WEAK, and none is reported as verified-clean.

proofOfAbsence: a test walks every .ts under lib/, strips comments, and fails if any of those names appear in code. verification-envelope.ts names them in prose only, to say they do not exist.
